A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoMixer study. All main sections, Figures 1–6, Tables 1–4, and Appendices A–B are available and readable. The shorter v3 reflects bibliography and layout changes, not missing scientific material.

before.justification: v2 reports original pretraining comparisons on eight reasoning benchmarks, checkpoint-selection ablations, training trajectories, and analyses of selected data in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental and data-analysis results, including Tables 2–4 and Figures 4–6.

M1.justification: Sections 3–5 retain the same checkpoint selection, DataInf approximation, embedding/output-layer scoring, top-50% regrouping, influence aggregation, and sampling weights. Appendix B and Algorithm 1 describe the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu and the same eight reasoning benchmarks listed in Section 6. No datasets, tasks, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed in the appendices.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains uniform, perplexity, and n-gram sampling comparisons with the same AutoMixer variants. Table 3 retains the last-checkpoint and 10-checkpoint alternatives. Bibliographic revisions do not change evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported zero-shot evaluation, model configurations, simulation budgets, sequence length, filtering threshold, and sampling procedures remain unchanged in Sections 4–6 and Appendix B.

E4.justification: The checkpoint-choice ablation in Table 3, training-trajectory analysis in Figure 4, proxy-size and sample analyses in Figures 5–6, and percentile statistics in Appendix A are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report two runs per configuration with distinct random initializations and retain the same plus/minus reporting in Tables 2–3. No additional seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical tests appear.

E6.justification: All table entries and plotted results match, including Table 2's reported AutoMixer-350M average improvements of 1.93%, 1.22%, and 1.05% at the three target model scales. Appendix A's Table 4 is also unchanged.

T1.justification: The influence definitions, Hessian-based expression, DataInf approximation, checkpoint blending, and group-weight equations are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about checkpoint-based data mixing, reusable proxy models, and performance improvements up to 1.93%.

C2.justification: Interpretations of checkpoint selection and proxy-size effects are unchanged. The limitations retain computational overhead, dataset bias, reasoning-focused coverage, and uncertain transfer across architectures and training scales.

D1.justification: v3 removes the linked FineWeb-Edu bibliography entry present in v2, leaving '?' citations in Table 1 and Section 6 and eliminating that dataset access link. Hardware, training costs, implementation details, and Appendix B remain unchanged.

R1.justification: References to Blakeney et al. (2024), Zhang and Others (2024), and Lozhkov et al. (2024) are removed. The surrounding research positioning remains unchanged. The reattributed DataComp-LM entry represents a revision of an existing reference rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: Edits mainly concern citations and bibliographic metadata, including DataInf's year, DataComp-LM's attribution and identifier, and Chang et al.'s venue. The main prose, terminology, and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 3–6 use higher-resolution images depicting the same content. Text, tables, references, and Algorithm 1 undergo modest spacing and pagination changes; the unchanged appendices move from page 12 to page 11.

improvement.justification: Higher-resolution figures and fuller DataInf metadata provide modest benefits. However, v3 removes the linked training-data reference, leaving '?' in Table 1 and Section 6, and replaces DataComp-LM's identifier with the incomplete 'arXiv:2401.XXXXX'. These visible source-traceability defects outweigh the limited presentation gains, producing a small decline in documentation reliability.
